extracted.intended_audience: USPTO patent examiners, OPLA staff, and practitioners handling merged reissue/reexamination proceedings (patent owners and third-party requesters)
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance on handling merged inter partes reexamination and reissue application proceedings: when and how to merge or stay proceedings, required notifications, permitted communications, amendment rules, effects of litigation and court decisions, fee handling, and examiner responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: OPLA notification when reissue filed during reexamination
rubrics_metrics.description: OPLA should be notified, as promptly as possible after the reissue application reaches the TC, when a reissue application is filed after an inter partes reexamination request has been filed (or when proceedings are ready for consideration of merger).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A determination will be made as to whether reexamination should be ordered. If ordered, no first Office action will accompany the decision-ordering reexamination. If any files are paper files, they should be hand delivered to OPLA at the time of the e-mail notification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Considerations for ordering merger
rubrics_metrics.description: In deciding whether to merge the reissue application examination and the reexamination proceeding, consideration will be given to whether the reissue application raises issues that would not be proper for consideration in reexamination and/or not proper for comment by the reexamination third party requester, and to the status of the reexamination proceeding (e.g., on appeal or Notice of Intent to Issue a Reexamination Certificate).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If issues not proper for reexamination are raised, merger ordinarily will not be ordered and one proceeding will be stayed. Status factors (appeal, NOI to issue certificate) weigh against merger.

rubrics_metrics.name: Maintaining identical amendments in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where merger is ordered, the patent owner is required to maintain identical amendments in the reissue application and the reexamination file for purposes of the merged proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If identical amendments are not present at time of merger, the patent owner must submit a housekeeping amendment placing the same amendments in both proceedings. The housekeeping amendment must not address any issue of patentability. Amendments in a merged proceeding are submitted under 37 CFR 1.173 per reissue practice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consequences of non-identical claims after merger
rubrics_metrics.description: If an amendment to make the claims the same in each file is required by the merger decision but is not timely submitted, any claim that does not contain identical text in all merged proceedings should be rejected under 35 U.S.C. 112, paragraph 2, as indefinite.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to place identical text in all files may trigger 35 U.S.C. 112, para. 2 rejections for indefiniteness (failing to particularly point out the invention).

rubrics_metrics.name: Handling of multiple copending proceedings (inter partes, ex parte, reissue)
rubrics_metrics.description: When inter partes reexamination, ex parte reexamination, and a reissue application are copending, OPLA should be notified promptly that proceedings are ready for merger consideration; paper files should be hand delivered where appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OPLA will decide whether to merge. Specific handling differs depending on chronological sequence (examples (A)-(C) provided). Merger of three proceedings will not be carried out pursuant to MPEP Chapter 2200; prosecution prior to merger remains as-is.

rubrics_metrics.name: No premature petitions to merge/stay before reexamination order
rubrics_metrics.description: No petition to merge or to stay is necessary and petitions filed prior to the determination (37 CFR 1.923) and order to reexamine (37 CFR 1.931) will not be considered and will be returned to the filing party by OPLA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returned petitions will be made of record in both files but no copy retained. This prevents premature papers relating to reexamination from being filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may petition to merge or stay after order to reexamine
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent owner may file a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 to merge or to stay after the order to reexamine; the third party requester may also file such a petition after the order to reexamine. Petitions by parties other than the patent owner or third party requester will not be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Any petition under 37 CFR 1.182 filed prior to the initial Office action on the merits must also be filed under 37 CFR 1.183 to waive the requirement of 37 CFR 1.933(b) that no paper be filed prior to the initial Office action on the merits of the inter partes reexamination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single fee treatment in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Where proceedings have been merged and a paper requiring payment of a fee is filed (e.g., excess claims fee, extension of time, appeal fees, briefs), only a single fee need be paid even though copies of the paper are filed for each merged file.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: only one fee need be paid for an appellant brief filed for merged multiple examinations. As to excess claim fees, reissue practice will control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interviews prohibited on merits in merged inter partes proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.955, an interview which discusses the merits of a proceeding is not permitted in an inter partes reexamination proceeding; therefore, in a merged proceeding of an inter partes reexamination and a reissue application, there will be no inter partes interview as to the substance and no separate ex parte interview as to the substance with either the patent owner or the third party requester.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a party requests information as to the merits, the examiner will not conduct a personal or telephone interview. Informal amendments by the patent owner will not be accepted because that would be tantamount to an ex parte interview. All communications directed to merits must be in writing and filed with the Office for entry into the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limitations on examiner’s amendments in merged proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Examiner’s amendments accompanying a Notice of Allowability in a merged reissue/inter partes reexamination proceeding are limited to matters that need no applicant authorization (formal matters, title changes, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Permitted: corrections of grammar, spelling, incorrect number, or title changes. All such amendments must be made by formal examiner’s amendment accompanying the Notice of Allowability to provide notice to both patent owner and third-party requester. Any change going to the merits cannot be made by examiner’s amendment and instead requires reopening with CRU Director approval, an Office action suggesting the change, a formal amendment submitted by patent owner, and an opportunity for third-party comment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory mandate for special dispatch
rubrics_metrics.description: Inter partes reexamination proceedings must be conducted with special dispatch within the Office (35 U.S.C. 314), unless otherwise provided by the Director for good cause.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Special dispatch applies including appeals to the Board. The statutory clause 'unless otherwise provided by the Director for good cause' permits stays in inter partes reexamination in circumstances of good cause (unlike ex parte reexamination).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expedited handling when court-ordered/sanctioned or litigation stayed
rubrics_metrics.description: When a request for reexamination indicates it is filed as a result of a court order or court-sanctioned agreement, or that litigation is stayed for reexamination, the request will be taken up by the examiner for decision 6 weeks after filing and all aspects will be expedited.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Office actions in these reexaminations will normally set a 1-month shortened statutory period for response rather than the usual 2 months. Response periods may be extended only upon a strong showing of sufficient cause. Such proceedings will generally take precedence over other examiner actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortened response periods for long-pending reexaminations concurrent with litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: If reexamination is concurrent with litigation and has been pending more than one year, the Director/Deputy Director of OPLA, CRU Director, or Senior Legal Advisor may approve Office actions setting a one-month or thirty days (whichever is longer) shortened statutory period for response instead of two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Approval is designated by a statement at end of Office action: 'One month or thirty days, whichever is longer, shortened statutory period approved,' followed by signature of an approving official.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of Federal Court decisions known at time of request determination
rubrics_metrics.description: If a Federal Court decision on the merits is known to the examiner at the time the determination on the request for inter partes reexamination is made, the examiner follows guidelines: the existence of a final court decision does not necessarily preclude a substantial new question; the Office will make its determination independently of the court's decision except a final holding of invalidity/unenforceability is controlling.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office may accord deference to factual findings by the court but will make its own determination of SNQ (substantial new question). Non-final holdings are not controlling. Only a final holding (after all appeals) of invalidity/unenforceability will preclude a SNQ as to the claims held invalid or unenforceable (Ethicon v. Quigg).

rubrics_metrics.name: Special rules when third-party requester was a party to prior litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: When the third-party requester was a party to the prior litigation, the provisions of 37 CFR 1.907(b) apply: a final decision adverse to the requester as to claim validity precludes that party (and privies) from requesting inter partes reexamination on issues raised or that could have been raised in the civil action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner must determine: (1) was the decision adverse to requester as to at least one claim; (2) was the decision final after all appeals; (3) is the issue in the reexamination request the same or could have been raised in the civil action. If all three are yes for all claims requested, the reexamination prosecution must be terminated and CRU Director will vacate the proceeding. If yes for some claims, those claims will not be treated and reasons noted in examiner’s action. If questions (1) or (3) are no for all claims, examination proceeds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effects of final court holding of invalidity vs validity
rubrics_metrics.description: A final holding of claim invalidity or unenforceability (after all appeals) is controlling on the Office; reexamination of those claims will continue until decision becomes final and then the claims held invalid/unenforceable will be withdrawn from consideration. Conversely, a final holding upholding validity where requester was a party may require discontinuance for affected claims under 37 CFR 1.907(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If all claims being examined are finally held invalid, CRU Director will vacate the reexamination as not containing a substantial new question. If a final holding upholds validity and 1.907(b) applies to all claims, the order to reexamine is vacated and reexamination terminated. Non-final court decisions have no binding effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedure when court decision issues after reexamination ordered
rubrics_metrics.description: Upon issuance of a holding of claim invalidity or unenforceability by a Federal Court, reexamination of those claims will continue in the Office until the decision becomes final; a non-final Court decision shall have no binding effect on reexamination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a final Court holding issues after all appeals, reexamination is reviewed to see if no substantial new question remains and 37 CFR 1.907(b) applies; claims held invalid are withdrawn from consideration and form paragraph 26.80 should be used at the beginning of the Office action to indicate claims not being reexamined.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mandatory notification of court decisions by patent owner
rubrics_metrics.description: Pursuant to 37 CFR 1.985(a), the patent owner in an inter partes reexamination proceeding must promptly notify the Office of any Federal Court decision involving the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prompt notification is required so the Office can review the reexamination in light of the court decision and take appropriate action (withdraw claims, vacate reexamination, or continue examination of remaining claims).

rubrics_metrics.name: Form paragraph 26.80 for claims held invalid by court
rubrics_metrics.description: When claims have been held invalid by a court and are no longer being reexamined, use form paragraph 26.80 to indicate: 'Claims [1] of the [2] patent are not being reexamined in view of the final decision of [3]. Claims [1] were held invalid by the [4].'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiner note provides insertion instructions for claim numbers, patentee name, decision citation, and court name. Use at the beginning of the Office action when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Guidelines on suspension/stay of inter partes reexamination due to litigation
rubrics_metrics.description: If a patent in the process of inter partes reexamination is or becomes involved in litigation, the Director shall determine whether to suspend the inter partes reexamination proceeding; for inter partes reexamination the Director may suspend for 'good cause' and such matters are approached case-by-case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Suspension will not be considered on merits prior to ordering reexamination. Suspension will not be considered on merits when there is an outstanding Office action unless the patent owner provides a complete response, includes a petition to suspend under 37 CFR 1.182, and includes a petition under 37 CFR 1.182 for OPLA to take jurisdiction prior to issuing an Office action and retain jurisdiction until decision on petition to suspend.
